answer: Give each agent a single hardware-bound identity: an enclave attestation proves one key per device, so a Sybil farm needs a warehouse of real chips, not just code. New identities start at the mesa — a flat, low transaction ceiling — and only climb toward the zenith of full throughput after months of clean, auditable work. Fraud anywhere sends a ripple through the vouching graph, slashing the stakes of every sponsor who vouched for the attacker. The cost is therefore physical hardware plus time plus lost collateral, while honest agents pay almost nothing beyond patience.
